dedupe_keys.name: internet shutdowns in iran autumn 2022 multi stakeholder technical measurement report

description: This report combines several network measurement datasets to document the internet shutdowns and censorship in Iran after the death of Mahsa Amini in September 2022. It is written by OONI, IODA, M-Lab, Cloudflare, Kentik, Censored Planet, ISOC and Article 19 as the first of a planned series of multi-stakeholder technical reports, analysing measurements from 16 September to 16 October 2022. Key findings: alongside years of pervasive censorship, new events included a digital curfew that shut down access to major mobile networks between 21 September and 3 October from 4 PM to midnight daily and again on 8, 12 and 15 October, and a wider range of technical strategies to prevent circumvention. Producer: the contributing measurement organisations, coordinated by OONI and ISOC and facilitated by the European Commission and the United States. Coverage: Iran. Access: a public web report on the IODA site. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence is stated on the page read. Caveats: the participants contribute only technical analysis and the report covers one country and one month; details of each dataset need to be taken from the sources cited within. Simulation uses: the observed outage timing and mobile versus fixed patterns can calibrate scenarios of deliberate loss of connectivity and its impact on network availability. Related record: IODA internet outage detection (data-ioda-internet-outage-detection), the data source used.
